answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. The protection comes from the fact that every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer, so flooding the jury floods the attacker with its own cost. Consider a umber as the anchor of the cost.
